title: Saturday, September 19, 2026
description: Three things for the desk: rates moved against buyers and the move is not finished, with the 30-year fixed back above 7% after the Fed's first hike since 2023 and another hike live, so anyone floating into a closing inside 45 days should have the lock conversation now; housing completions fell 27.1% year over year in August, which is next year's inventory shortfall visible a full twelve months early and belongs in every hold-versus-sell conversation this quarter; and builder sentiment at 32 with Lennar cutting its full-year delivery target to 80,000-81,000 homes means new construction is where the negotiating leverage sits, with August existing and new home sales printing late next week. And three things for the world: the FOMC raised the federal funds target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September, unanimously, under Chair Kevin Warsh; crude is holding above $95 a barrel and US diesel near $6.40 a gallon with the Strait of Hormuz under active attack, which is the inflation story behind the rate story; and the SEC approved a five-year conditional innovation exemption for tokenised assets, repricing the entire crypto complex in a single session.

title: Friday, September 18, 2026
description: Three things for the desk this Friday, 18 September 2026. One: the Federal Reserve raised rates on Wednesday to a target range of 3.75 to 4.00 percent, and the daily 30-year mortgage now sits at 7.19 percent, just five basis points off its twelve-month high, while Freddie Mac's weekly survey still reads 6.95 percent — get ahead of that gap with clients before your lender has to explain it. Two: new home completions fell 27.1 percent year over year in August to an annual rate of 1,128,000, so builder incentives on finished stock are real right now but have a shelf life — a concrete reason for a hesitant buyer to move this autumn that does not depend on predicting rates. Three: KB Home reports third quarter results on Tuesday 22 September and the federal government funding deadline is 1 October; both can move sentiment inside two weeks. Also in this episode: August housing starts at 1,275,000 and the widening mortgage spread, Egypt's Sisi hosting Abbas in Cairo ahead of the UN General Assembly, the Supreme Court blocking mail ballot restrictions, Wednesday's equity close and the oil and gold moves, Practical Magic 2 taking the box office with 30 million dollars, and Real Madrid's 3-2 escape at Elche.

title: Tuesday, September 15, 2026
description: Three things for the desk: Anchor property tax relief payments roll out in New Jersey this week, so get ahead of the client question. The Fed decides tomorrow afternoon and the market is pricing a hike rather than a cut, so anyone floating a rate today is taking a live position on it, and mind the gap between the 6.76 percent Freddie Mac survey your clients read in the paper and the 7.17 percent daily tracker they get quoted at the closing table. And New Jersey's August figures show supply up 6.9 percent and closed sales down 2.4 percent while homes still close at 101.8 percent of list, a seller's market loosening at the edges, so price to that rather than to last spring. And three things for the world: the Federal Reserve may raise rates tomorrow, with oil above 100 dollars a barrel the reason; the Iran war has moved into the shipping lanes, with a vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf talks postponed and a Saudi pipeline shut; and the AI slowdown argument went political in a single weekend, with Dario Amodei calling for a pause, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis agreeing, and the White House and the Speaker of the House saying no. Also inside: Emmy night, Monday's chip-led selloff, and Mourinho's Madrid past Rayo four-one.

title: Monday, September 14, 2026
description: Three things for the desk: The Fed announces Wednesday with a fresh dot plot, and futures are pricing better-than-even odds of a hike rather than a cut, so ring your rate-locked buyers today rather than Thursday. The daily tracker has the thirty-year fixed at 6.88 percent while Freddie Mac's weekly survey says 6.76 percent, a twelve basis point gap that exists because the survey is weighted to Monday-through-Wednesday responses and missed the late-week back-up in yields, so have that explanation ready before a client quotes you the lower number. Manhattan's top end signed just thirteen luxury contracts in the week before Labor Day with nothing above ten million dollars, so price a trophy listing to the Fed this week, not to the spring. And three things for the world: oil is back above one hundred dollars a barrel with American diesel at a record six dollars and six cents a gallon, which is the inflation story sitting underneath the Fed's problem; a Russian drone struck the Kyiv-to-Warsaw train near the Polish border in a nationwide barrage that killed six and injured forty-three; and Sweden's centre-left has won by a single seat, leaving the far-right Sweden Democrats apparently locked out of government. Also inside: a 785 million dollar Manhattan office loan to special servicing against a 131 million dollar Nutley office trade, Oracle's 95 billion dollar capex lifting Dell and HPE, Practical Magic 2 topping a quiet 81.6 million dollar box office weekend, and Real Madrid 4-1 Rayo Vallecano with a Mbappe double.

title: Sunday, September 13, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One: the Federal Reserve decides at two o'clock on Wednesday the sixteenth — no cut is expected and some forecasters still see a hike, so any client sitting on a float needs to choose before Wednesday, not after. Two: requote everybody — the daily tracker is at 7.12 percent while the Freddie Mac headline says 6.76 percent, and that 36 basis point gap is the most likely source of an awkward conversation this week. Three: existing home sales fell 2 percent in August to a 3.98 million annual rate, below the four-million mark, with inventory building — sellers need a pricing conversation now, not in October. And three things for the world. One: core inflation fell to 2.4 percent, the lowest since March 2021, but headline inflation is stuck at 3.4 percent on petrol prices. Two: Saudi Arabia has shut its main East-West pipeline after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory, with Iran the prime suspect, just as oil had been falling. Three: the eighteenth BRICS summit is under way in New Delhi with India in the chair, and the US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks have slipped to October.

title: Saturday, September 12, 2026
description: Three things for the desk today. First, and this is the deadline, the Federal Open Market Committee meets Wednesday the sixteenth and the market now puts a quarter point rate hike at ninety percent after Friday's inflation report, up from seventy percent the day before, so spend Monday and Tuesday on your rate sensitive pipeline and lock everything that can be locked before the committee speaks. Second, your clients are reading six point seven six percent from Thursday's Freddie Mac survey while daily quotes stood at six point nine eight percent annual percentage rate on Friday, up nineteen basis points in a single day, so explain the difference between a note rate and an annual percentage rate to every active buyer this week before the lock desk explains it for you. Third, the ten year Treasury closed the week at four point nine six percent, a fifty two week high, and the mortgage to Treasury spread is back to a historically normal one hundred and eighty basis points, so there is no abnormal spread left to deflate: underwrite new deals to a seven handle, and with existing home sales down two percent in August, price new listings to sell rather than to test the market. And three things for the world. First, yesterday was the twenty fifth anniversary of the September the eleventh attacks, marked at Ground Zero, the Pentagon and Shanksville. Second, American inflation is running at three point four percent a year, hotter than forecast, with gasoline up twenty seven point four percent over the year doing more than a third of the monthly damage. Third, Brent crude closed a week above one hundred dollars a barrel for the first time since May on Middle Eastern tension, which is precisely why the inflation number looked the way it did. Also in this episode: core inflation at two point four percent, the National Association of Realtors reporting August existing home sales down two percent, industrial commercial mortgage backed securities issuance picking up, Friday's market rebound inside a losing week, Real Madrid beating Inter Milan two goals to one to open the Champions League, and New Jersey's Governor under pressure over allegations against her Lieutenant Governor.

title: Thursday, September 10, 2026
description: Three things for the desk today. First, the Federal Reserve meets Wednesday the sixteenth and markets put a rate hike at better than a coin flip, around fifty-six percent on CME FedWatch, so ring your rate-sensitive buyers and lock anything that can be locked before the meeting rather than after it. Second, the daily thirty-year fixed is six point eight one percent while the Freddie Mac survey number your clients will read is six point seven one, so close that expectation gap yourself in advance or the market will close it for you mid-negotiation. Third, Jersey City's August median hit seven hundred and eighty-eight thousand dollars, a new high for the quarter, but only forty-five percent of homes sold at or above asking and days on market rose to twenty from seventeen, so price new listings to sell rather than to test. Also in this episode: open US-Iran conflict with Brent crude above one hundred and two dollars, the UK, France and Canada banning trade with Israeli West Bank settlements, Wednesday's market close, the twenty-fifth anniversary of September eleventh and New York City opening its records, and Real Madrid beating Inter Milan two goals to one to open the Champions League.

title: Saturday, September 5, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One, the deadline: the 25th anniversary of September 11th falls this Friday, with an expanded New York City commemoration and heavy security in Lower Manhattan, so move or pad any downtown showings, closings or client meetings now rather than Thursday night. Two, change your rate script: the 30-year fixed is at 6.71 percent, a 13-month high, and the spread over the 10-year Treasury has compressed to roughly 194 basis points, close to historically normal, so the free improvement is gone and further mortgage relief now requires the 10-year itself to fall, which Friday's hot jobs print pushes against. Three, test the multifamily bid: 36.7 billion dollars of transaction volume in the first half, a Denver deal at about 390,000 dollars a door, and agency debt visibly flowing in the Seattle trade all say it is time to go back to apartment sellers who have been holding out since 2024. And three things for the world. One, Jose Mourinho is back as manager of Real Madrid, appointed in June on a deal through 2029, and has taken them top of La Liga with three straight wins. Two, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has the biggest opening weekend in cinema history and is only the second film ever to pass 900 million dollars in North America. Three, the Missouri Supreme Court has unanimously blocked the Republican-drawn congressional map from November's midterms, a real complication for a very tight fight for the House.

title: Thursday, September 3, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One, the FOMC meets 15-16 September, twelve days out, so lock or float decisions on anything closing inside three weeks should be made this week; note the 30-year fixed sits about 210bp over the 10-year against a long-run norm nearer 170bp, so a Treasury rally will not pass through one-for-one. Two, underwrite Q4 on today's rates: August private payrolls came in at 38,000, the softest since January, and the 10-year still did not rally, meaning oil and supply are pricing the long end rather than the Fed. Three, if you have multifamily to bring to market, bring it now: 36.7 billion dollars traded in the first half, agency debt is still writing cheques as the 20.6 million dollar Freddie Mac loan on the Seattle trade shows, and rising sale-leaseback volume means competing product is coming. And three things for the world. One, the United States struck Iran on 1 September, Iran retaliated across Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq, and four American service members were confirmed killed; that conflict is now the biggest single input into the oil price. Two, the House rejected a constitutional amendment to cap the Supreme Court at nine justices, 212 votes to 206. Three, Real Madrid spent roughly 200 million pounds this summer, released Dani Carvajal after 451 appearances, and have opened the season with three wins from three.

title: Tuesday, August 25, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One: Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed Chair on Friday 28 August at 10am ET — have the lock conversation with floating clients today or tomorrow, not Thursday afternoon. Two: quote the daily tracker at 6.77%, not the Freddie Mac weekly survey at 6.65% — the survey lags and clients arrive with the wrong expectation. Three: the mortgage spread is 207 basis points against a historical norm nearer 170, so the next third of a point of relief comes from spread compression rather than a Fed cut; and on commercial, price to today's debt cost — a Washington DC office tower at 1250 Connecticut Ave NW just went to foreclosure sale. Also in this episode: Treasury Secretary Bessent's "Operation Economic Outcast" sanctions campaign against Iran and Tehran's threatened Strait of Hormuz toll, with Brent at $94.12; the Supreme Court lifting one of two injunctions on the mail-in voting executive order ahead of the midterms; a mixed Monday tape with the Nasdaq down 0.8% on a chip sell-off ahead of Nvidia's Wednesday print; NJ Transit's 3% July fare rise and Mayor Mamdani's Brooklyn-Queens Expressway move; the weekend box office led by Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $39m; and Real Madrid opening La Liga with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, Carlos Espi scoring a stoppage-time winner on debut under new manager Jose Mourinho.

title: Monday, August 24, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One: Freddie Mac's next survey lands Thursday, so you have three days — rates are at 6.65 percent and easing gently, but Kevin Warsh has just debuted at Jackson Hole into a market debating hike risk rather than cuts, so any client waiting for materially cheaper money this autumn is waiting on something the market is not pricing; have that conversation before Thursday. Two: the Northeast median is up 5.2 percent year over year against a national 2.0 percent — more than double, the strongest regional gain in the country — so put it in your next listing presentation and seller conversation this week. Three: inventory sits at 4.6 months and days on market have ticked up to 29, with a quarter of the market paying cash, so reset seller expectations now rather than in October. And three things for the world. One: Kevin Warsh has given his first Jackson Hole address as Fed Chairman, and the live argument is about a possible hike, not a cut. Two: Iran has threatened to halt oil exports entirely and its parliament is advancing tolls on the Strait of Hormuz as Washington readies what Scott Bessent calls an economic D-Day, with Brent near 94 dollars. Three: Bitcoin just had a 22 percent week, and Spider-Man has held the box office top spot for a fourth straight weekend.

title: Friday, August 14, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. The thirty-year fixed fell to 6.67 percent, its first drop in six weeks, and borrowers are moving on tiny changes, so call the fence-sitters today. New Jersey price reductions are up nearly 20 percent year over year with inventory up 14 percent, so have the pricing conversation with sellers in week one, especially in Bergen and Morris, while Sussex runs the opposite way. And New York's pied-a-terre fight is live with the tax possibly rolling out during appeal, so clients eyeing a Manhattan second home above five million dollars need advice now. Also inside: the September Fed debate is about a hike rather than a cut, the Strait of Hormuz is still barely open, the S&P 500 cleared 7,800 for the first time, Spider-Man: Brand New Day passed a billion, and Real Madrid signed Yan Diomande for a club record.

title: Saturday, August 8, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac's revised condo project standards are landing this month, eliminating the limited review path and lifting reserves to 15% of budget — confirm the effective date with your lender Monday and assume a full review on every August and September condo closing. Two: the daily 30-year tracker sits at 6.91% while Freddie Mac's Thursday survey printed 6.69%, a 22bp gap the wrong way round, so get ahead of the client who quotes you the lower number. Three: the September Fed question is a hike, not a cut — Friday's weak jobs report bought borrowers time, not a rally, so expiring locks should close today. And three things for the world. One: US employers cut 23,000 jobs in July with a further 103,000 revised off prior months, unemployment at 4.1%, and the S&P 500 hit a record 7,757 precisely because weak data cools rate-hike odds. Two: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a mutual defence pact in Mecca with an attack-on-one-is-an-attack-on-all clause, in the middle of the Iran war, with Hormuz traffic down to 33 vessels from 50. Three: the Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and sent it to the House, targeting buyers of Russian oil. Also inside: Vinicius Junior extends at Real Madrid to June 2032, Spider-Man Brand New Day's $355m opening and a record $429m weekend, and the Port Authority's $45bn capital plan.

title: Friday, August 7, 2026
description: Three things for the desk. One: the survey and the screen disagree — Freddie Mac has the thirty-year fixed at 6.69 percent and a one-year high, while the Mortgage News Daily index has it at 6.75 percent and drifting lower for a fortnight, so any buyer who read the AP headline needs that explained before they cancel a weekend viewing. Two: the mortgage spread is doing the damage, not the Treasury — roughly 2.1 percentage points over a 4.63 percent ten-year, which is wide, so price your conversations for rates staying in this neighbourhood through the autumn rather than promising a break. Three: institutional and household money have decoupled — Manhattan investment sales ran 10 billion dollars in the first half, up 50 percent, while residential mortgage demand has fallen below year-ago levels. Also in this episode: the Trump-Hegseth Camp David row over Iran munitions, the Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz corridor and the oil whipsaw, Abdul El-Sayed's upset win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, Erica Schwartz confirmed as CDC director 51-44 amid a 35-year measles high, Austria's back-to-back national heat records, a record-setting week on Wall Street that lost its nerve on Thursday, Mamdani and the Mayor's Fund, the biggest box office weekend in history, and Real Madrid's club-record signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig.
